name: MAPK Pheromone Response Pathway (Detailed)
description: The mating pheromone response in S. cerevisiae is a prototypical GPCR-MAPK signaling cascade. α-factor (MATa cells) or a-factor (MATα cells) binds to the GPCR Ste2 or Ste3, activating the heterotrimeric G-protein (Gα Gpa1, Gβγ Ste4-Ste18). Free Gβγ recruits scaffold Ste5 to the membrane, which assembles the MAPK module: Ste11 (MAPKKK), Ste7 (MAPKK), Fus3/Kss1 (MAPK). Phosphorylated Fus3 activates transcription factor Ste12 (relieving Dig1/2 repression), induces mating genes (FUS1, FUS2), arrests cell cycle in G1, and triggers polarized growth toward mating partner. The pathway includes multiple feedback loops and checkpoints to ensure commitment to mating. This expanded flowchart illustrates the complete cascade from pheromone binding through cell fusion, highlighting scaffold function, crosstalk prevention, and the extensive AND gate requirements for eukaryotic MAPK signaling.
scientificAccuracy: Based on decades of research on yeast mating pathway, a paradigm for MAPK signaling. All components validated.

notes: MAPK mating pathway shows very high AND gates (10) - paradigm for eukaryotic signal transduction. Scaffold (Ste5) ensures specificity. Multiple checkpoints require AND logic.
